questions.prompt: Why store data in a file instead of a variable?
choices: A variable is gone when the program ends; a file is still there next time
Files use less memory while the program runs
questions.explain: Everything in memory disappears when the process exits. Persistence is the whole reason files exist.

questions.prompt: What makes a file a text file rather than a binary file?
choices: Its contents are characters you could read in a text editor
questions.explain: The distinction is the encoding, not the extension. A .csv and a .py are both text; a .jpg opened in an editor is noise.

questions.prompt: Put the file handling workflow in the order the lesson gives it.
items: Open the file, choosing a mode
Read from it or write to it
questions.explain: Nothing can be read or written before the file is open, and the changes are not guaranteed to be on disk until it is closed.

questions.prompt: Which of these are text files?
questions.explain: A .csv is rows of characters separated by commas, so it is text. An image and an executable are bytes that only make sense to the program that reads them.

reflection-exercise1.hint: Name the kind of thing being stored, and say what would be lost if the program only kept it in a variable.

reflection-exercise2.hint: Give real extensions for each side, and say what tells the two kinds apart when you open one.
